{{Quote|Yearo Seville, the pirate who now lends credibility to his atrocities by calling himself a political rebel, has taken credit for the abduction and is demanding a huge ransom.|News anchor|<ref name="TA" />}}
'''Yearo Seville''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] and a member of the [[Seville Family|Seville pirate clan]] during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He had nine parallel scars on his cheek. During Seville's youth, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[MdZ-BLK]] tried to [[Death/Legends|kill]] its owner, the Seville matriarch [[Darion Seville]]&mdash;who was also Yearo's mother&mdash;but Yearo saved her and disposed of the droid, sending it to kill [[Gorbu Dalo]], a rival [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]]. Seville was also involved in the abduction of [[Crying Dawn Singer]], a [[Shashay]] cultural hero. The operation was only one of the many moves in an important conspiracy of [[Braig Farool]], [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Narg]], to depose and replace [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Nile Owen]] of the [[Rayter sector/Legends|Rayter sector]]. The pirate then allied himself with agents of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to annihilate the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of the rival [[Vallaido Clan|Vallaido pirate clan]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|That's right, we've got him, and if you want him back, you've got to pay our price.|Yearo Seville, in a ransom recording|<ref name="TA" />}}
Yearo Seville, a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], was the [[Parent/Legends|son]] of [[Darion Seville]], the matriarch of the [[Seville Family|Seville pirate clan]]. Darion liked to have her [[Droid/Legends|droids]] fight each other, but during one such duel, the droid [[MdZ-BLK]] attempted to [[Death/Legends|kill]] her. Yearo intervened and [[Ion blaster/Legends|ionized]] the droid, saving his mother's life. Afterward, he sent the droid as a gift to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Gorbu Dalo]], a rival [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]], in the hope that the droid would kill Dalo. MdZ-BLK indeed murdered the Hutt, but the droid then stole a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]], loaded it with explosives, and sent it to crash against the [[Seville family compound]]. Seville, however, was not killed during this attack.<ref name="cro" />

Seville, an ambitious person, joined a ring of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and killed more than one hundred [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] before he was fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old. Eventually, he created his [[Yearo Seville's pirate gang|own pirate gang]] and obtained a [[Yacht/Legends|space yacht]] he called ''[[Seville's Star]]''. At some point, Seville also owned and customized a [[VR-10 Cuirilla-Rayl Xylines-class spacetug|CRX-Tug]], which had been prepared to accept a [[Limb/Legends|one-legged]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]. Seville then sold the Tug to a procurement [[Officer/Legends|officer]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], claiming that the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] had been used in [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] and that it retained secret information in its memory. However, Seville was lying, and the [[Memory bank/Legends|memory core]] had been fused. The Alliance then christened the ship ''[[Worthless Fool]]''.<ref name="TA" />

[[File:SevilleAbduction1-TA.png|thumb|left|250px|Seville abducts Crying Dawn Singer.]]
Circa [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], Seville was approached by [[Nak Farool]], Special Assistant to [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Nile Owen]] of the [[Rayter sector/Legends|Rayter sector]]. Farool was looking for a [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrel]] who could kidnap [[Crying Dawn Singer]], a [[Shashay]] cultural hero, and then pretend to be a leader of the Alliance to Restore the Republic asking for a ransom. This would stall [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] meetings between the Alliance and the Shashay. Once this was done, Seville had orders to hand over the Shashay to the Galactic Empire. Farool would then stage a charade of a rescue, and the Empire would gain notoriety among the Shashay, while Seville would receive [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]] for his services.<ref name="TA" />

However, Nak Farool conspired along with his brother, [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Braig Farool]] of [[Narg]], to depose and replace Moff Owen with this plot. Nak Farool ordered Seville to take Crying Dawn Singer to Narg and deliver him to Farool, instead of to Owen. Seville accepted the conditions and kidnapped Crying Dawn Singer and his entourage during the opening of the [[Sector Performing Arts Center]], using an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] provided by Farool. Seville took his [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] to an Imperial base on [[Najarka]] and [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] them to death, except for Crying Dawn Singer, who survived, and the droid [[KL-6TLF7V/T|KL-6T-LF7V/T]], who was only disconnected. KL-6T-LF7V/T was identified as an undercover Rebel agent, and Seville was asked to leave it at Najarka, where Owen would pick it up while the pirate took Crying Dawn Singer to the [[Laim system/Legends|Laim system]].<ref name="TA" />

Once in Laim, Seville recorded a [[Hologram/Legends|holotransmission]] asking for an unacceptable ransom as he had been ordered to. He also battered Crying Dawn Singer and claimed to be a leader of the Rebel Alliance. The message was broadcast, along with several other forgeries of Nak Farool, but the Alliance tracked it to Laim. The Shashay, however, believed the message to be true, and threatened to go to Moff Owen if the Alliance failed to return Crying Dawn Singer. Seville then took Crying Dawn Singer to Narg and handed the Shashay over to Farool. At this point, members of the Rebel Alliance were following Seville's steps in an attempt to recover Crying Dawn Singer.<ref name="TA" />

{{RPG|''[[The Abduction]]''}}
His mission accomplished, Seville left Narg. Farool's implication was discovered by the Alliance and by Owen, and he was harassed by agents of his many enemies. Farool lost his mind and, megalomaniacally, believed that he had disgraced Seville, the Alliance, Owen, and all the [[Sector/Legends|sectorial]] powers. The Rebellion rescued Crying Dawn Singer from the hands of the governor, and the Shashay took up diplomatic relations with the Alliance again.<ref name="TA" />
{{Endgame}}

Still at large, Seville made a deal with the Galactic Empire. The Empire agreed to reinforce the Seville clan [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] in an [[Raid against the Vallaido fleet|attack]] against the fleet of the [[Vallaido Clan|Vallaido pirate clan]], who had been enemies of the Sevilles for generations. While the Vallaido fleet was destroyed, a number of Vallaidos survived. One of these survivors was [[Siro Simito]], who decided to join the Alliance to Restore the Republic in response to Seville's actions.<ref name="cro" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:SevilleAbduction2-TA.png|thumb|right|Seville claiming to be a Rebel leader]]
{{Quote|Okay boys, let's do it.|Yearo Seville, giving orders to kidnap a target|<ref name="TA" />}}
A dark-haired Human male with a mustache, Seville had nine parallel scars on his left cheek. He could also be identified because he enjoyed eccentric, lavish clothes and because he used a [[Gold/Legends|gold]]-plated [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and a [[drommanarg]] snuff pouch. Although he was not particularly tall or burly, he was threatening in his careful composure. Ruthless and greedy, Seville was known to manipulate his subordinates into paranoia for his own safety. He was considered the most sanguinary and wicked outlaw in the Rayter sector.<ref name="TA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Yearo Seville first appeared in ''[[The Abduction]]'' ([[1992]]), a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The book included Seville's roleplaying statistics. According to those, Seville was a skillful crewman and was not specialized in any responsibility except command, but was apt for several of them. He was also a good fighter in both close and long distances, and was excellent at intimidating and conning people. However, the adventure included no situation in which Seville was entitled to use these skills, as the player characters never really meet him in person. Seville disappears from the plot after leaving Narg, and as such there are no alternate paths affecting him.<ref name="TA" />
